rationales: Cl₂ and O₂ have nonpolar covalent bonds because each bond is between identical atoms.
N₂ has a nonpolar bond, although H₂O has polar covalent bonds.
C₃H₈ is generally treated as having nonpolar covalent bonds, although H₂O has polar covalent bonds.
Both HCl and H₂O have polar covalent bonds.
Group 1 and Group 2 elements belong to the s-block.
The p-block contains Groups 13 to 18.
The d-block contains the transition elements.
The f-block contains the inner transition elements.
A beta particle is an electron or positron, not a helium nucleus.
A He²⁺ nucleus is an alpha particle.
A gamma particle is electromagnetic radiation, not a nucleus.
A helium nucleus has a positive charge and is not neutral.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Phosphorus is not characteristically lustrous.
Sulphur is not characteristically lustrous.
Hydrogen is a gas and is not lustrous.
Eight electrons correspond to four shared pairs, not a triple bond.
A triple covalent bond contains three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Four electrons correspond to two shared pairs, as in a double bond.
Three electrons do not make a covalent triple bond, which uses six shared electrons.
Volume per mass is not the stated mass of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
Volume per volume expresses the volume of solute per volume of solution.
Mass per volume expresses grams of solute per 100 cm³ of solution for this percentage.
Mass per mass uses the mass of solution rather than its volume.
Cations are positively charged ions, not shared bonding electrons.
Anions are negatively charged ions, not shared bonding electrons.
A shared pair of electrons that forms a chemical bond is called a bond pair.
A lone pair is not shared to form the bond.
Zinc is not the metal typically identified for jewelry because of the stated characteristics.
Sodium is highly reactive and is unsuitable for ordinary jewelry items.
Platinum is durable, lustrous, and valued for making jewelry.
Lead is toxic and unsuitable for jewelry items.
Z denotes the atomic number, not the mass number.
P may represent the number of protons, not the mass number.
n denotes the number of neutrons, not the mass number.
A is the symbol for mass number.
Rutherford is widely regarded as the father of nuclear science.
Bohr is known for his atomic model, not as the father of nuclear science.
Newton is known for classical mechanics, not nuclear science.
Dalton is known for atomic theory, not nuclear science.
Atomic radius generally increases, rather than decreases, from right to left across a period.
Ionization energy generally decreases from right to left across a period.
Electron affinity generally decreases from right to left across a period.
Electronegativity generally decreases from right to left across a period.
The s subshell is the valence subshell for Groups 1 and 2, not Groups 13 to 18.
The valence electrons of Groups 13 to 18 occupy p subshells.
The d subshell is associated with transition elements.
The f subshell is associated with inner transition elements.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer, not mutual sharing.
A covalent bond forms by mutual sharing of valence electrons.
A metallic bond involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
A coordinate bond is a covalent bond in which one atom supplies both shared electrons.
A percentage is one way to express the proportion, but the general term is concentration.
Concentration describes the proportion of solute in a solution.
Molarity is one specific measure of concentration, based on moles per litre.
Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves under specified conditions.
H₂ is diatomic, not triatomic.
O₃ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
H₂O contains three atoms and is triatomic.
CO₂ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
